items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: And one time his lip went bad, and I think we sent in your own, he didn't got Tommy Ladnere. And Red Allen. Oh, another time we had Red Allen playing with us.

ctx.x: Did you happen to record with Fess Williams? I was there, they made, uh, one record in the name of Fess and his Joy Boys or something. But that might have been earlier. No, I think that was some of the, that was a little earlier.

I think that's when he first came from Louisville. Oh yeah. I made arrangements, the first arrangements I made to be recorded were made for Red, uh, what's Red's name? You know his brother played trombone? Red, huh?
Oh gosh, I can't think of his name.

items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: I went to the Regal Theater in 1929 and we had a wonderful band there. We had Red Top playing trumpet

ctx.x: You started as an arranger, didn't you? No, I started, I started playing violin. I was with this man playing violin. Well, I mean with your writing though, you started with the banjo. Uh-huh.

And, uh, the banjo became so prominent, prominent that I got a banjo. And, uh, then I went to the Regal Theater in 1929 and we had a wonderful band there. We had Red Top playing trumpet and he was later with Cab Callaway, he was playing a tremendous trumpet.

items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: Red Temple was. No, and Red played the second trumpet in the shows and on the band numbers... I know who you're talking about.

ctx.x: Oh gosh, I can't think of his name.

Isn't that awful. What did Red play? Trumpet. You see we had Fats Robin that played the straight trumpet. Red Temple was. No, and Red played the second trumpet in the shows and on the band numbers and on the dance numbers where they, we had, we had to play for dancing couples or dancing singles. Why, Red played the first trumpet and he took off, jazzed it up and I mean he really, he really played. I know who you're talking about. Yeah, I know you do.
